concerns.text: Task T012a (Spec Amendment) is placed AFTER T010/T011 (Tests) and T012 (Implementation). The implementation T012 explicitly relies on the amended FR-001 (30 trajectories). A consumer (T012) cannot precede its producer (the amended spec requirement in T012a). The spec amendment must be the first task in Phase 3 to establish the valid requirement before any code or tests are written.

Task T036a (Spec Amendment for GLMM) is placed AFTER T035 (Wilcoxon implementation) and T036 (GLMM implementation). T036 explicitly implements the 'amended FR-005'. The task ordering violates the producer-before-consumer rule: the spec amendment (producer) must precede the implementation of the new statistical method (consumer). T036a must move before T035 and T036.

Task T017a (Spec Amendment removing human-in-the-loop) is placed AFTER T017b (Implementation of expert-system validator). T017b implements a validator based on the 'amended FR-007'. The task ordering creates a circular dependency where the implementation precedes the requirement change it relies on. T017a must precede T017b.

Task T007 (Create base ExecutionLog data model) is placed AFTER T005 (memory_profiler) and T008 (validator). T005 and T008 likely require the ExecutionLog structure to log results. While T005 logs to a JSON file, T008 validates trajectories which may need the data model. More critically, T022 (Phase 4) and T033 (Phase 5) explicitly depend on 'ExecutionLog'. T007 should be moved to the very start of Phase 2 (Foundational) to ensure the data model is available for all subsequent foundational and user-story tasks.

Task T012a is marked [P] (parallel-safe). However, it amends the spec (FR-001) which is a shared artifact consumed by T012 and potentially T016/T017. Spec amendments are not parallel-safe if other tasks in the same phase depend on the *new* state of the spec. T012a should not be marked [P] if it blocks the start of T012.
